**No** — `CatalogApi.CreateItem` does not publish `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` (or any integration event).

What `CreateItem` actually does (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-388`):

1. Takes `[AsParameters] CatalogServices services` and a `CatalogItem product` from the request body (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-368`).
2. Constructs a **new** `CatalogItem(product.Name)`, copying `Id`, `CatalogBrandId`, `CatalogTypeId`, `Description`, `PictureFileName`, `Price`, `AvailableStock`, `RestockThreshold`, and `MaxStockThreshold` from the posted product (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:370-381`).
3. Computes and assigns an AI embedding via `await services.CatalogAI.GetEmbeddingAsync(item)` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:382`).
4. Adds the item to `services.Context.CatalogItems` and calls `await services.Context.SaveChangesAsync()` — a plain EF Core save, with no `services.EventService` usage and no local transaction/outbox logic (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:384-385`).
5. Returns `TypedResults.Created($"/api/catalog/items/{item.Id}")` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:387`). It is declared to return `Task<Created>` and is annotated `[ProducesResponseType<ProblemDetails>(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest, ...)]` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:365-366`). It is mapped to `POST /items` as route name "CreateItem" (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:103-106`).

How I established the "no": a repo-wide search for `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` shows the only publish site in Catalog.API is inside `UpdateItem`, not `CreateItem` — it fires only when the price property `IsModified`, saving via `services.EventService.SaveEventAndCatalogContextChangesAsync` and then `PublishThroughEventBusAsync` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:345-357`). The event type itself is defined at `src/Catalog.API/IntegrationEvents/Events/ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent.cs:6` and is consumed by Webhooks.API (`src/Webhooks.API/IntegrationEvents/ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:3`). A search for `CreateItem` found only one definition in the codebase (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366`), so there is no other overload that could publish the event.
